articles.title: Former NFL coach Rex Ryan charged after allegedly hitting pedestrians with car in Nashville
articles.summary: Former Jets and Bills coach turned himself in. Ryan faces six misdemeanor charges over incident. Two pedestrians allegedly struck in Nashville. ESPN analyst and former NFL coach Rex Ryan turned himself in to police on Wednesday after allegedly hitting two pedestrians with his car in Nashville and…
body: Nashville police said on Wednesday that the pedestrians had the right of way while crossing a main street in the city’s downtown last week when Ryan allegedly turned at a red light and drove over their feet.

Ryan was charged with two counts of leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failing to provide information or render aid and two counts of failing to obey a traffic control signal, according to court records. All six charges are misdemeanors.

Ryan, 63, served as head coach of the New York Jets from 2009 to 2014 and the Buffalo Bills from 2015 to 2016. He led the Jets to consecutive AFC championship games following the 2009 and 2010 seasons.
His father, the late Buddy Ryan, was a celebrated NFL coach who served as defensive coordinator of the 1985 Chicago Bears, whose defense is widely regarded as one of the greatest in league history.

articles.title: Marco Rubio reportedly spent over $1.2m of taxpayer money traveling to son’s football games
articles.summary: Ethics watchdogs question necessity of the US secretary of state flying between DC and Gainesville so often. Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, has emerged as a superfan of the University of Florida ’s football team, spending more than $1.2m of taxpayers’ money on frequent personal trips to…
body: Ethics watchdogs have questioned the necessity of the country’s top diplomat shuttling so often between Washington DC and Gainesville, where his son Anthony has a walk-on role as a running back for the team known as the Gators.

An investigation by the Washington Post found that Rubio has attended at least 10 games in the last two seasons, including five this fall, and that of 23 total trips made to Gainesville on military aircraft, 15 were “personal” in nature.

The newspaper said that while Rubio is prohibited from flying commercially, because of security protocols that also cover the secretary of defense and FBI and CIA directors, his use of government transport “appears to significantly outpace that of his predecessors”.
Using published defense department rates listing the cost per hour of different kinds of military aircraft, the Post calculated that the flights alone have cost more than $1.2m.

articles.title: Shrewsbury 'hit all the boxes' for new owners - Friedel
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview with BBC Radio Shropshire new Shrewsbury Town sporting director Brad Friedel says the club is a perfect fit for the new owners.
body: Shrewsbury Town's new sporting director Brad Friedel says the club is the perfect project for the US-backed owners after a Europe-wide search ended with them taking contol of the League Two outfit.

Scott Davidson's Biscayne ST LLC consortium, which Friedel is part of, completed their takeover on Monday, buying 87.4% of the shares and allowing long-time owner Roland Wycherley to relinquish control.
"Scott and I met through friends in Miami and through the love of football and nothing more or less," former Blackburn and USA goalkeeper Friedel told BBC Radio Shropshire in an exclusive interview.
"As we got to know each other, our thoughts on business and football aligned - we got to the point where we said let's try to find a club which fits a whole bunch of criteria.

articles.title: Top four teams in Fifa rankings set to be kept apart until semi-finals at 2027 Women’s World Cup
articles.summary: Team must win World Cup group to trigger rule. Spain, US, Germany and England currently in top four. The top four-ranked teams will be separated until the semi-finals at the 2027 Women’s World Cup, provided they each win their group, after a change to the tournament’s draw procedure was confirmed…
body: Spain, the United States, Germany and England are currently ranked one to four in the world respectively, although the US and England still need to qualify for the tournament. The seedings will be based on 7 December’s updated rankings, meaning the standings could change before the draw, which will take place on 11 December in Rio de Janeiro.

The top four sides were also separated until the semi-finals of the 2026 men’s World Cup, which consisted of 48 teams, but it was not announced until Wednesday that the same rule would apply to the 32-team women’s tournament. In the men’s World Cup the top four – Spain, Argentina, France and England – all reached the semi-finals.

Record four-time champions the US face El Salvador on 27 November as they bid to confirm their place at next summer’s tournament. A victory, coupled with no changes to the world rankings, would ensure the Americans would be placed in the opposite half of the draw to the defending champions, Spain. That would mean if they win their groups the two teams could not meet until the final, which will be played at the Maracanã Stadium on 25 July. Neither Spain nor the US finished top of their group at the last World Cup.

articles.title: ‘Hear the goals during the afterlife’: Barça fans get to inter ashes at club’s new memorial
articles.summary: Memorial FC Barcelona, part of upgrade to Camp Nou stadium, will consist of 26,000 niches where fans can deposit their ashes. Lifelong supporters of Barcelona football club will soon be able to cheer on the club from beyond the grave – but, like everything else at Barça, eternal devotion comes at a…
body: As part of an upgrade to the Camp Nou, the club has inaugurated the Memorial FC Barcelona, consisting of 26,000 niches where fans can deposit their ashes after their own final whistle has blown.

Supporting the team from the afterlife will cost €2,490 (£2,082) for 10 years or €6,000 for 50 years, with an annual maintenance fee of €70. Guaranteeing your niche for eternity will set you back €10,000, with a further €490 for a memorial plaque.

Presenting the Memorial FC Barcelona, María Elena Fort, the club’s institutional vice-president, said: “When my grandfather died many years ago, he said the only thing he wanted was to be buried next to Barça’s pitch so that he could hear the goals go in during the afterlife. Many fans dream of the same thing.”

The memorial, designed by the architect Quique Montoya, will consist of four large illuminated squares, while the memorial plaques will be installed in a glass wall backlit with LED lights. The urns will be kept behind a mural commemorating key moments in the club’s 125-year history.

articles.title: Legally restrict heading a football in training, says MP
articles.summary: An MP is calling for legal safeguards to limit repetitive heading in football training, amid growing concerns about the risk of brain injury.
body: Grahame Morris, the Labour MP for Easington, submitted a parliamentary motion on Tuesday urging the government to take action to reduce the number of times a player can head the ball in training.
Researchers have found footballers are three and a half times more likely to die from a neurodegenerative disease than the general population.
The Early Day Motion (EDM) describes the need to protect players' brain health as a "significant public health and player welfare issue".

"The aim of this EDM is to raise awareness of the growing body of evidence linking repeated head impacts, particularly from heading a football, to an increased risk of neurodegenerative disease," Morris told BBC Sport.

articles.title: Could King really become 'one of the best players in the world'?
articles.summary: Josh King was always one of the best players in his age group. "Nationally," clarifies Charlie Turnbull, his coach in Fulham's academy for five seasons between his U10 and U14 years, to Sky Sports. But there was another quality that set him apart.
body: "One of the most outstanding things about Josh is that whenever the level went up, whenever there was a pressure game, he loved it," adds Turnbull. "He loved it when things got hard. He loved it when there was a little bit of extra pressure.

"He wanted it. He wanted to feel like the pressure was on him and the responsibility was on him to produce for the team. He enjoyed that. You always saw the best of Josh when the ante was up. I never once saw him not deliver in those circumstances.

"We would play tournaments in France, Spain and Portugal, against the giants of Europe, and afterwards the staff from each club would have to pick the best player they'd seen across the weekend. I remember Josh winning that accolade more than once."

King's temperament now forms part of his appeal to Thomas Tuchel, who called him up for England ahead of Cole Palmer and Phil Foden. "It's the attitude and the personality," he said last week. It all bodes well ahead of a possible debut against Croatia or Spain.

articles.title: Jones: Japan aiming to 'make Twickenham sky fall in on distracted England'
articles.summary: Former England head coach Eddie Jones has said his Japan side are aiming to "make the Twickenham sky fall in on" Steve Borthwick's "distracted" charges in Saturday's Nations Championship Test.
body: Jones, who oversaw England between 2016 and 2022, before being dismissed a year before the 2023 Rugby World Cup in France after a calendar year saw just five victories and England fans booing the side following defeat to South Africa.

The 66-year-old has since returned to Australia for an ill-fated and short second reign which ended in a first-ever World Cup pool stage exit for the Wallabies, and then returned as Japan head coach in 2024.
Ahead of his Brave Blossoms side facing England at Twickenham on Saturday, Jones has sought to stoke the flames.

"We're massive underdogs," Jones told the BBC. "We've got to find a way to disrupt an England side that's looking at New Zealand next week [Saturday November 21] and sometimes may be a little bit distracted.

articles.title: No excuses as Pocognoli seeks first Hampden victory
articles.summary: Having lost his first two home matches, Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli needs to deliver a convincing win against North Macedonia, writes Tom English.
body: For Sebastien Pocognoli, Friday against North Macedonia is a third opportunity to replace the Hampden Bore with something akin to a Hampden Roar.
Two home games so far under the new head coach and two defeats; five goals conceded, one scored.
The loss to a superior Switzerland was written off because of an early red card for Jack Hendry. The loss to Slovenia had no such mitigation.
Scotland were creatively bereft, physically weak and tactically confused. Captain Andy Robertson said that his team had been out-played and out-fought.

articles.title: Kane targets biggest team prizes ahead of record-breaking England cap
articles.summary: Harry Kane will become England's record appearance maker on Thursday night - but the Ballon d'Or winner now has his sights set on the biggest team trophies in football.
body: England captain Kane will win his 126th cap for his country against Croatia in the Nations League at Wembley. The landmark moment comes just weeks after he was crowned the best player in the world.

But while the striker has ended his long wait for team glory with back-to-back Bundesliga titles at Bayern Munich, as well as a German Cup, he is now eager to kick on again and land the most prestigious prizes for club and country.

"To win a team trophy with England, a major trophy, is my biggest dream," he said in a press conference on Wednesday when asked what comes next for him. "That's always been my biggest dream, to win a European Championship or a World Cup, or both, hopefully, but I know how difficult that is. Extremely motivated to do that.
"Individual accolades are incredible and things I'm proud of but ultimately they're a consequence of trying to make the team better and trying to win something with the team.
